bib.title: GLIDE: Towards Photorealistic Image Generation and Editing with Text-Guided Diffusion Models

question: Can guided diffusion models produce photorealistic text-conditional images, and which guidance (CLIP or classifier-free) works better?
hypothesis: Classifier-free guidance will beat CLIP guidance on human-judged photorealism and caption match, because CLIP guidance exploits the evaluation CLIP model.
contributions: 3.5B text-conditional diffusion model with CF guidance preferred by humans over DALL-E
Comparison of CLIP guidance (noised CLIP) and CF guidance
Release of a 300M filtered model (GLIDE filtered) and a noised ViT-B CLIP

method.summary: A 3.5B ADM-style 64x64 diffusion model with a transformer text encoder plus a 1.5B 64->256 upsampler, trained on the DALL-E dataset; fine-tuned for CF guidance (20% empty captions) and for inpainting (extra 4 input channels). Compared with noised-CLIP guidance and DALL-E by FID and human Elo/win rates.

datasets.name: DALL-E training dataset
datasets.source: same dataset as Ramesh et al. 2021; size not stated

datasets.name: GLIDE (filtered) dataset
datasets.source: internet, largely disjoint from CLIP and DALL-E data
datasets.preprocessing: people, violent objects and hate symbols (swastika, confederate flag) filtered by SVMs on CLIP ViT-B/16 features at <1% false negative rate

datasets.name: MS-COCO validation
datasets.split: validation; entire validation set as FID reference

models.name: GLIDE base
models.architecture: ADM ImageNet 64x64 architecture, width 512 channels, text tokens fed via final-token embedding as class embedding and concatenated into attention context

models.name: GLIDE upsampler
models.architecture: ADM ImageNet upsampler, 384 base channels, text encoder width 1024

models.name: Noised CLIP ViT-L
models.architecture: ViT, patch 4x4, 64x64 input, image encoder f(xt,t)

models.name: GLIDE (filtered)
models.architecture: small version on filtered data; upsampler 192 base channels, 512 text encoder channels

other.sampling: temp 0.85 and 1.0, CLIP reranking best of 256 (Fig 5) or 512 (App G)

training.objective: Lsimple noise-prediction MSE with learned variance (Nichol & Dhariwal 2021)
training.steps: 2.5M iterations base; 1.6M upsampler; CLIP 390K + 30K finetune; GLIDE (filtered) 1.1M + 500K finetune; filtered upsampler 400K
training.compute: roughly equal to DALL-E training compute (no number)

other.cf_finetune: after pretraining, fine-tune with 20% of captions replaced by empty sequence
other.inpaint_finetune: random regions erased; 4 extra input channels (second RGB set + mask) zero-initialised; upsampler gets full low-res image but only unmasked high-res
other.noised_clip: same objective as CLIP, 50-50 mix of CLIP and DALL-E datasets, same noise schedule as base model

inference.decoding: diffusion sampling; CF guidance eps_hat = eps(xt|empty) + s*(eps(xt|c)-eps(xt|empty))
inference.samples: 30,000 prompts for FID; no reranking or cherry-picking for GLIDE

parameters.upsampler_steps: 27 via 5 segments of 10,10,3,2,2 evenly spaced steps; found by sweeping FID on internal validation

metrics.name: FID
metrics.definition: 30k generated vs entire MS-COCO validation set, center-cropped

metrics.name: Elo (photorealism, caption)
metrics.definition: Bradley-Terry style Elo fit from pairwise human wins; ties count half; sigma init 0; minimises -sum A_ij log(1/(1+10^((s_i-s_j)/400)))

metrics.name: Win probability vs DALL-E
metrics.definition: share of human pairwise comparisons won, ties half

metrics.name: CLIP score
metrics.definition: E[s(f(image).g(caption))], s = CLIP logit scale 100, CLIP ViT-B/16

eval.protocol: Humans see two 256x256 images and pick better caption match or more photorealistic, or neither. 1,000 comparisons each (500 for guidance-scale sweeps). Number/identity of raters, payment and interface not stated. No significance tests or seeds reported.

availability.weights: only the small filtered 300M model and noised ViT-B CLIP

evidence.quote: we trained a ViT-L with weight decay 0.0125

results.claim: Human raters prefer GLIDE (classifier-free guidance) to DALL-E on photorealism.
results.setup: Introduction headline; GLIDE 3.5B with CF guidance vs DALL-E, MS-COCO captions, 256x256
results.quote:
preferred to those from DALL-E (Ramesh et al., 2021) 87% of the time when evalu-
ated for photorealism, and 69% of the time when evaluated
for caption similarity
results.note: Matches Table 3 row 'DALL-E reranked, temp 0.85' (87% photorealism, 69% caption). Quote spans a line break in the cache.

results.claim: Against DALL-E with no reranking at temp 1.0, GLIDE wins photorealism 91%.
results.table: Table 3, row No reranking temp 1.0, column Photorealism
results.note: Caption similarity 83% in same row; temp 0.85: 84% and 80%.

results.claim: Against DALL-E reranked (temp 0.85), GLIDE wins caption similarity 69%.
results.table: Table 3, row DALL-E reranked temp 0.85, column Caption Similarity

results.claim: Even with DALL-E reranked and GLIDE outputs passed through DALL-E's dVAE (blurred), GLIDE still wins, by smaller margins.
results.setup: Table 3 last rows, temp 0.85 photorealism; caption 61%; temp 1.0: 72% and 63%
results.table: Table 3, row DALL-E reranked + GLIDE blurred, temp 0.85, column Photorealism

results.claim: Classifier-free guidance gets the best human Elo for photorealism (scale 3.0) versus CLIP guidance (scale 2.0) and unguided.
results.table: Table 1, row Classifier-free guidance, column Photorealism

results.claim: Zero-shot MS-COCO 256x256 FID of GLIDE with CF guidance scale 1.5.
results.setup: 30k captions sampled, compared to entire validation set, center-cropped, CF scale 1.5, 250 diffusion steps
results.table: Table 2, row GLIDE, column Zero-shot FID
results.note: Trained-on-COCO baselines are better or similar: XMC-GAN 9.33, LAFITE 8.12 (not zero-shot).

results.claim: Purging validation images similar to training images raises FID only slightly.
results.quote:
We ﬁnd that our FID increases slightly from 12.24
to 12.89 in this case

results.claim: CLIP guidance raises CLIP score more than CF guidance, but humans disagree; authors hypothesise CLIP guidance finds adversarial examples for the evaluation CLIP model.
results.quote:
We hypothesize that CLIP guidance is ﬁnding adversarial
examples for the evaluation CLIP model
results.note: Hypothesis, not tested directly beyond human eval.

results.claim: CF guidance gives a larger Elo boost than scaling the model about 10x.
results.setup: 3.5B at scale 3.0 photorealism 133.0 vs 3.5B unguided -23.9; 300M scale 4.0 28.2 vs unguided -131.8
results.quote:
classiﬁer-free guidance gives a
larger Elo boost than scaling the model by roughly 10x

results.claim: GLIDE matches DALL-E training compute with a much smaller model and no reranking.
results.setup: 3.5B GLIDE (2.3B visual + 1.2B text encoder) vs DALL-E 12B
results.quote:
but with a much smaller model (3.5 billion vs. 12 billion
parameters)
results.note: Compute equality is stated as 'roughly'; no FLOP figure.

results.claim: Sampling latency of the unoptimised model.
results.quote:
takes 15 seconds to sample one
image on a single A100 GPU

results.claim: Fine-tuning for CF guidance replaces 20% of captions with the empty sequence.
results.setup: Fine-tuning of base model after pretraining (not trained with dropout from scratch)
results.quote:
20% of text
token sequences are replaced with the empty sequence

limits: Fails on highly unusual objects or scenarios (Fig 8).
Slow: 15 s per image on one A100, far slower than GANs.
Optimizer, learning rate, hardware, dataset size and exact compute not stated.
Human eval details (raters, interface) not stated; no confidence intervals.
Filtered 300M model keeps and may amplify dataset biases (e.g. toys for girls, Western stereotypes); biases amplified by CF guidance.
Released filtered model still retains inpainting, with misuse potential.
Filter is calibrated to two US hate symbols only, Western bias.
Adversarial-example explanation for CLIP guidance is a hypothesis.

terms.definition: replace the label with a null label with fixed probability in training; at sampling extrapolate from the unconditional toward the conditional prediction by scale s >= 1
CLIP models trained on noised images xt so gradients are correct during diffusion sampling

lineage.work: Diffusion models beat GANs on image synthesis (ADM)

lineage.note: basis of noised CLIP and CLIP score
inpainting fine-tuning similar to Saharia et al.

figures.why: Shows CLIP guidance wins CLIP score but loses on FID, motivating the human eval.
